# AI/LLM Integration

Covers dimension 11 (AI/LLM Integration) of the Temporal evaluation.

## Overview

Temporal is not an AI platform — it is a durable execution engine that
has been increasingly adopted for AI agent orchestration [20][37]. The AI
integration story is "run your AI code as Activities" rather than "use
our built-in AI nodes" [38].

## OpenAI Agents SDK Integration

Temporal partnered with OpenAI to add durable execution to the OpenAI
Agents SDK [20]:

| Milestone | Date | Source |
|-----------|------|--------|
| Public Preview | July 30, 2025 | [20] |
| General Availability | March 23, 2026 (Python SDK) | [20] |

The integration works by executing each agent invocation as a Temporal
Activity [20]. The OpenAI Runner class was refactored as an abstract base
class, allowing Temporal to provide a concrete implementation [20]. Key
capabilities:
- Automatic recovery from crashes (resume from last checkpoint) [20]
- Rate-limit handling (retry when LLM capacity returns) [20]
- Network resilience (retry downstream requests) [20]
- Horizontal scaling (each micro-agent in its own process/thread) [20]
- Cost savings (no redundant token usage on recovery) [20]

## MCP (Model Context Protocol) Support

Temporal implements MCP tools as durable Temporal Workflows [21]:

- MCP tools gain automatic retries, fault tolerance, and long-running
  capability [21]
- Tools persist beyond individual agent sessions [21]
- Existing Temporal workflows become immediately usable as MCP tools [21]
- Official MCP server implementations available, bridging AI assistants
  (Claude, GitHub Copilot) with Temporal workflows [41]
- Supports Go, Java, Python, .NET [21]

The "Durable MCP" concept adds reliability guarantees that standard MCP
lacks [21].

## AI Patterns in Temporal

### Durable Agent Loop
LLM invocations happen in Activities (non-deterministic); the Workflow
orchestrates the loop deterministically [38][35]:
- Automatic state management across hours/days/months [35]
- Automatic retries for probabilistic LLM responses [35]
- Human-in-the-loop via Signals for approving LLM decisions [39]

### Multi-Agent Architectures
Two patterns documented [36]:
1. **Agent Routing**: Switching between specialized agents based on context
2. **Task Delegation**: Specialist team approach with coordinator

### Available Examples
Official AI cookbook and samples [18][38][39][40]:

## Industry Positioning

Temporal joined the Agentic AI Foundation as a Gold Member in December
2025 [34], positioning itself as infrastructure for production AI agents.

## Relevance to PA Use Case

For the PA (personal AI-assisted engineering assistant), Temporal's AI
integration is **not directly relevant**. The PA is the LLM layer (Claude
Code); the workflow engine runs deterministic pipelines (shell commands,
CLI tools). The PA does not need the workflow engine to invoke LLMs —
it needs the engine to reliably execute scheduled CLI tasks.

However, the MCP integration [41] could be relevant: Temporal workflows
could be exposed as MCP tools that the PA discovers and calls, providing
a standardized interface between Claude Code and the automation layer.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No native LLM nodes or built-in AI primitives — AI integration is "write
  code that calls LLM APIs in Activities."
- MCP server implementations appear to be community-maintained rather than
  officially supported Temporal products [41].
- The Pydantic AI integration [35] is a blog post pattern, not a supported
  SDK feature.
- AI cookbook examples are Python-focused; other SDK coverage is sparse.
